_note: Editorial sidecar for tools/build-cert-regulation-pages.mjs. The register (infant-instruments.json) is exported from the Heavy Metal Index regulatory register and MUST NOT carry editorial prose — a re-export would clobber it. This file holds the small set of things the generator cannot derive from the register: each instrument's legal NATURE (binding law / guidance / reference standard), and the CURATED, one-way cert→index cross-links (the firewall permits outbound citations to heavymetalindex.com only; the cert site never imports index pages). Every field is optional; the generator produces a complete page from data alone when an entry is absent. index_regulator/index_deepdives hrefs were verified 200 on 2026-08-09.

index_regulator.label: European Commission on the Heavy Metal Index

index_deepdives.label: EFSA — the tolerable intakes these levels rest on

eu-2023-915.scope_extra: It is the broadest infant and child food set tracked here and, alongside Brazil, the most complete: six of the eight HMTc metals carry a level, and it is the only tracked instrument to set an infant-relevant nickel level.

index_regulator.label: European Commission on the Heavy Metal Index

uk-1881-2006.scope_extra: It is the pre-2023 EU contaminants framework assimilated into Great Britain law at withdrawal, so its levels track the earlier EU text rather than the current Regulation (EU) 2023/915.

index_regulator.label: Codex Alimentarius on the Heavy Metal Index

index_deepdives.label: JECFA — the FAO/WHO expert body behind the Codex levels

codex-cxs-193.scope_extra: Codex levels are not law in any single country; they are the FAO/WHO baseline that national limits are written against and measured by, which is why a low Codex count can still anchor a global reading.

canada-contaminants.scope_extra: Health Canada carries contaminant limits by reference under the Food and Drug Regulations rather than in a single consolidated table, so its tracked infant and child food set is narrow.

china-gb-2762.scope_extra: GB 2762 is unusual in tracking total arsenic and total chromium alongside the inorganic-arsenic and lead levels most bodies set, so it appears in comparisons where few others do.

india-fssai.scope_extra: The FSSAI set is one of the few tracked instruments to carry a total-arsenic and a tin level for infant and child food, and its lead level sits above the 10 µg/kg most bodies converge on.

brazil-anvisa.scope_extra: ANVISA RDC 722/2022 is, with the EU, the broadest infant and child food set tracked here, covering the same six metals across a wide span of product categories.

gso-193.scope_extra: GSO 193 is the Gulf Standardization Organization contaminants standard adopted across the GCC states; only its infant and child food lead level is tracked here.

au-nz-fsanz.scope_extra: The Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code is the only tracked instrument to set an infant-relevant aluminium level, and it states arsenic as total rather than inorganic.

index_regulator.label: US FDA on the Heavy Metal Index

index_deepdives.label: FDA Closer to Zero — 10 ppb lead action level for baby food

us-fda-c2z.scope_extra: Closer to Zero action levels are guidance, not binding maximum levels: they signal the concentration at which the FDA may act, and the United States sets no binding food maximum level for these metals.
